title: Teaching AI to Find Real Vulnerabilities — Prof. David Brumley, Bugcrowd
talk_summary: Brumley describes how to design RL/eval environments for vulnerability discovery, arguing that single-bug tasks cause reward hacking and that deterministic oracles (crash/backtrace uniquification) beat LLM-as-judge. He then shows a 16-rung capability ladder on V8 where crash-triggering saturates across models but full sandbox escape separates them sharply.

takeaways.technique: Deterministic oracle instead of LLM-as-judge for pass/fail
takeaways.what_they_do: Grade agent success by an executable check (did the program crash, did the exploit run) rather than asking a model whether it succeeded.
takeaways.evidence_quote: The LLMs will always say they were successful hacking. And so, what you want to come up with is a deterministic grading oracle

takeaways.technique: Precision/recall over a set, not single-target pass
takeaways.what_they_do: Ask for all findings, uniquify them, and score precision (valid/submitted) and recall (found/known) multiplicatively so spamming and easy-target farming both lose.
takeaways.evidence_quote: precision versus recall is the way to balance those two competing goals
takeaways.numbers: 50% of DARPA hand-curated challenges had unknown bugs; AIxCC had 18 unintended bugs found

takeaways.technique: Capability ladder to localize where the model fails
takeaways.what_they_do: Bucket a hard task into 16 graded rungs (trigger, primitive, chain, full exploit) so failure yields signal about which capability is missing.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we bucketized 16 different capabilities in a ladder
takeaways.numbers: Crash-trigger: GPT/Mythos 95%, Gemini/Kimi/GLM ~50%; full ACE: Mythos 73%, GPT 68%, Gemini/Kimi 0%

takeaways.technique: Cheap-model saturation check before paying for frontier
takeaways.what_they_do: Shows that on easy rungs cheap models match frontier, so capability differences only appear on hard rungs; measure per-rung before choosing a model.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you were looking at the old benchmarks, the message would be 50% of the time Kimmy succeeds
takeaways.numbers: Kimi/Gemini/GLM ~50% on crash vs 0% on full exploit

takeaways.technique: Open-world task framing (don't tell the agent the answer exists)
takeaways.what_they_do: Withhold the hint that a bug exists and how many, so the model can't just target the one known issue and must reason over the whole program.
takeaways.evidence_quote: The model actually never knows how many vulnerabilities

takeaways.technique: Containerized reproducible environments with MCP interface
takeaways.what_they_do: Each task is a Docker image exposing setup/read/write/grade via MCP, so runs are reproducible across hosts and versions.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we like to enclose these inside container environments so that they're reproducible
